entries.title: A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT
entries.venue: anthropics/formal-math GitHub repository, eth/ directory (paper dated 2026-10-26, 49 pages; added in commit 16a5ce4 at 2026-10-27T03:07Z)
entries.claim: 3-SAT and k-SAT in time 2^{O(min{k^2 n log log n / sqrt(log n), k m / sqrt(log m)})}; the paper claims that ETH is therefore false. Lean defines ETH : Prop := 0 < s 3 and ETHIsFalse := not ETH on Mathlib Turing.FinTM2 and proves MainResults.ethIsFalse and MainResults.mainTheorem.
entries.relevance: Independent, near-simultaneous claimed refutation of ETH, not yet reviewed by experts. The formal statement is about ETH itself on Mathlib's standard TM2 model, which makes it the closest formal anchor for any ETH premise here; a bridge to the repository's one-tape model is still required.
entries.caveats: The repository README warns that no machine checks that the Lean file says what the paper says, so the fidelity of s 3 to textbook ETH needs human audit. The condensed key-idea section rederives only 2^{delta n} for every delta > 0. Crossover points are astronomically large (majdoddin-2026-crossovers). The paper states (Corollary 5) that the result also refutes SETH and gives E^NP circuit lower bounds via Williams; neither SETH nor the E^NP consequence is formalized. The 2026-10-16 discovery date and the 14M output-token figure come from the paper's own Provenance paragraph: 'The core algorithm was found on October 16 by an internal Claude research model with 14M output tokens and no human input.'
